messages:
oncall-bot: Incident created: elevated 429s observed from Hugging Face during model artifact pulls affecting fresh pod startups. Alert triggered by artifact-fetcher (>10% cold-start failures) at 1950012345.

sara: noticed spike after a deployment and scale event. New pods fail on `GET /llm-team/model-prod/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin` with 429s. Existing hot replicas keep serving. Autoscaler keeps creating nodes which then fail to fetch. Impact: scale-up events and scale-to-zero warmups. Customers on sudden traffic spikes might see increased 502s while we spin up. :rotating_light:

mike: digging into node logs — HF responses include `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` and `Retry-After` headers. This looks like provider-side throttling, not our auth. Example from node-7: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 20
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
{"error":"Too many requests"}
```

alex: runtime here. Short-term mitigations: 1) disable scale-to-zero for affected deployment(s) 2) switch resolver to internal mirror if we have a prefetched copy 3) fallback to `model-prod-quant` for cold starts. I can flip a feature flag for mirror resolver.

jamie: CS note: notifying top-tier customers with potential scaling patterns. Emphasize that existing sessions unaffected; only new instance initialization. Preparing short status blurb for status.redwood.ai.

infra-bot: Observability snapshot saved: s3://redwood-incidents/1950012345/snapshot.json. Prefetch capacity available on nodes: node-3,node-14.

mike: proposing automated prefetch job to download the model into our S3 artifact cache and update runtime to consult mirror first. If HF is returning account-level rate limits, mirroring reduces HF hits. I'll spin a k8s job.

sara: also recommend temporary rate-limit circuit breaker in runtime: after 3 consecutive 429s within 60s, mark model as "throttled" and move to fallback. We should page infra if it persists.

alex: applied feature flag `artifact_mirror_priority=true` at 1950013500 for the cluster. K8s batch job created: 
```
kubectl apply -f jobs/hf-prefetch-prod.yaml
image: infra/prefetcher:stable
args: ["--model","llm-team/model-prod","--dest","s3://internal-artifacts/hf/llm-team/model-prod/"]
```

infra-bot: Prefetch job started on nodes [node-3,node-14]. Download progress logged. Checksums verifying. Upload to internal S3 mirror completed (12m).

mike: Reconfigured deployment to `scale_to_zero: false` while mirror rolls out. Also configured autoscaler to prefer warm pool.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused automatically due to artifact fetch failures in 2/5 canary pods. Manual hold enacted.

alex: switched runtime resolver for new pods to `s3://internal-artifacts/hf/llm-team/model-prod/` at 1950014200. Old behavior remains for in-memory caches.

mike: metrics update: artifact-fetch 429 rate down from ~25/min to ~3/min after mirror fallback. Cold-start failure rate dropped from 16% to ~2.1%. Autoscaler stabilized.

jamie: status update posted: "Mitigation: temporary internal mirror and fallback model enabled. We are monitoring. No SLA breaches identified at this time." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1950012345

sara: opened support ticket with Hugging Face including logs and rate limit headers. Ticket HF-79012. Asked for temporary quota increase and explanation for sudden throttling patterns.

mike: quick config note — added an alert rule: 
```
alert: ArtifactFetchThrottled
expr: sum(rate(artifact_fetch_response{code="429"}[1m])) > 5
for: 2m
labels: {severity="page"}
```
This will page infra oncall.

alex: runtime changes to implement: - circuit breaker on repeated 429s - metric `artifact_fetch.rate_limited` exported - prefer mirror for scale events - fallback to quantized model automatically for cold starts. I'll open a PR against runtime.

infra-bot: Diagnostic bundle for postmortem uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1950012345/diagnostics.tar.gz

jamie: CSMs updated customer list and individual messages sent to impacted accounts. Monitoring for any follow-ups.

sara: handing to next oncall. Please keep HF ticket and status page updated. If HF says account-level automated throttling, escalate with account rep and consider paid artifact-hosting (CDN/mirror) as durable mitigation. Postmortem assigned.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty handoff: sara -> mike -> alex at 1950015600.

mike: follow-ups: schedule automated nightly prefetched sync for top 20 models; add test that simulates HF 429s during canary to ensure failover works; update runbook to include mirror fallback steps and contact matrix for HF rep.

alex: PR opened: runtime#482 to implement mirror-first resolver and circuit breaker. Adding unit tests and a metric.

jamie: posting incident summary to internal #incidents-postmortems with timeline and action items. No critical customer escalations yet.

sara: incident status -> mitigated, monitoring. Postmortem due within 72h. Assigned owners: sara, mike, alex, jamie. Closing thread for now. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
